card.name: Subject just before a past-tense verb
card.fires_on: A subject word (he, had, quickly, a name) right after a time or place clause in a biography, where a verb about what the person did is expected. Also fires on 'had' or 'has' before a result in study text.

modes.label: Biography narrative
modes.description: A pronoun or name after a clause about a career stage, where the next word is an action verb.
modes.example: the French and Indian War, where<< he>> served alongside a future opponent, George Washington

modes.label: Study findings
modes.description: A drug name or auxiliary verb right before a reported result.
modes.example: In two-year studies conducted in mice and rats, nabumetone had<< no>> statistically significant tumorigenic effect.

card.writes: It promotes Chinese verbs meaning show, display, demonstrate, so it expects a verb describing what the subject did or showed.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a life story or study report where a verb saying what someone did or showed comes next.
